{{Quote|The Nine Ruling Families are like any other families. Blood and merit create siblings and cousins and ranking distants. Some are released, others are rematched, others are born to trial. The same as any other family.|Aide Chaf'ees'aklaio, to Dean Jinzler|<ref name="Survivor's Quest">''[[Survivor's Quest]]''</ref>}}
The '''Ruling Families''', or the '''Ruling Houses''',<ref name="TEA" /> also known as the '''Nine Ruling Families''', the '''Nine Families''',<ref name="Survivor's Quest" /> the '''Four Families''',<ref name="Force Heretic II">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic II: Refugee]]''</ref> and at various points there were as many as twelve and as few as three Ruling Families,<ref name="Outbound Flight">[[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']]</ref> were a group of [[Chiss family/Legends|Chiss families]] that governed the [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss Ascendancy]].<ref name="TEA" /> Their representatives composed the [[Council of Families]].<ref name="CSWE Council of Families" /> Each of the Ruling Families were associated with a specific [[Color/Legends|color]] worn on the shoulder patches of the [[Defense Fleet uniform]]s of their [[Chiss officer/Legends|officers]] and [[Chiss warrior/Legends|warriors]].<ref name="Outbound Flight" />

==Description==
Each Family was responsible for a certain sector of Chiss government,<ref name="Gamer 5">{{GamerCite|5|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Chiss}}</ref> and each had formal representatives with titles such as [[Aristocra/Legends|Aristocra]] and [[Syndic/Legends|Syndic]].<ref name="Survivor's Quest" />

===Family ranks===
In order of least to greatest privilege within a Ruling Family, Chiss family ranks were:

*[[Merit adoptive/Legends|Merit adoptive]]<ref name="Outbound Flight" />
*[[Trial-born/Legends|Trial-born]]<ref name="Outbound Flight" />
*[[Ranking distant/Legends|Ranking distant]]<ref name="Outbound Flight" />
*[[Cousin/Legends|Cousin]]<ref name="Survivor's Quest" /> 
*[[Sibling (Chiss)|Sibling]] (brother or sister)<ref name="Survivor's Quest" />

A family rank of [[shadow child]] also existed, which kept an individual with that rank completely secret, to prevent the complete extermination of a Ruling Family by their enemies.<ref name="Dark Nest I">''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]''</ref>

While it seems that these titles often indicated literal blood relationships, they could also be awarded on merit, and while each Family was ultimately a kin-group, they also contained adoptive members who were not born into the oligarchy.<ref name="Survivor's Quest" /> For example, all [[Chiss warrior/Legends|Chiss warriors]] were classed as [[Merit adoptive/Legends|merit adoptives]] of a Ruling Family for the duration of their service in the [[Chiss Defense Fleet]] or [[Chiss Expansionary Fleet/Legends|Chiss Expansionary Fleet]], while being named as [[Trial-born/Legends|Trial-born]] of a family enabled the most able commoners to aim for permanent "[[Rematching/Legends|matching]]" to one of the Families. In rare cases, a Trial-born matched to the Family might even secure the status of ranking distant.<ref name="Outbound Flight" />

===Household Phalanxes===
Each Chiss Ruling Family had a fleet of [[Warship/Legends|warship]]s used as planetary defense forces for a homeworld affiliated with that family referred to as Household Phalanxes.<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref> The most well-known one was a personal [[Syndic Mitth'raw'nuruodo's Household Phalanx|Household Phalanx]] of Syndic [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]].<ref name="Vision of the Future">''[[Vision of the Future]]''</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|At various times over the centuries there have been as many as twelve and as few as three.|[[Force Commander]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]] on the history of the Ruling Families|<ref name="Outbound Flight" />}}
According to the ''[[The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life]]'' made available through [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] channels during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] Ruling Families traced their origins to the distant past, before the onset of the [[great ice age]] in which [[Csilla/Legends|Csilla]] had been gripped throughout reliably-recorded Chiss history, and it was implied that every contemporary Chiss individual had a blood relationship with at least one of the Families. The same sources, however, made clear that the information available at this time about pre-glaciation Csilla took the form of contradictory legends, and it is not clear how reliable the claims for the antiquity of the Families could therefore be.<ref name="Gamer 5" /> Secondly, and especially bearing in mind the dubious nature of this first claim, the idea that all five trillion contemporary Chiss could then trace some form of biological descent to no more than nine pairs of historical ancestors must ''prima facie'' be treated with extreme caution.

Over the course of recorded history, the number of Ruling Families was said to have fluctuated between three and twelve, but in contacts with the Chiss in<ref name="Outbound Flight" /> both [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]]<ref name="Outbound Flight date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of [[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']] to [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]].</ref> and [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]],<ref name="Survivor's Quest date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Survivor's Quest]]'' to [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]].</ref> it appeared that the number of Ruling Families stood nine, and they were known formally as the '''Nine Ruling Families'''.<ref name="Outbound Flight" /><ref name="Survivor's Quest" /> In 22 ABY,<ref name="Survivor's Quest date" /> the issue on preemptive strikes along with their [[defensive-only doctrine]] became a subject of strenuous debate among the Nine Ruling Families. In the same [[Standard year/Legends|year]], [[Aide/Legends|Aide]] [[Chaf'ees'aklaio]], core name "Feesa," of the [[Chaf family/Legends|Fifth Ruling Family]] explained to [[Dean Jinzler]] how the Nine Ruling Families were set up. Feesa described how the family ranks were structured and how they could be granted based on merits alone, or by blood.<ref name="Survivor's Quest" />

Within a few years of the latter date, it was said that the number of Ruling Families had been reduced to four, identified as [[Csapla family|House Csapla]], [[Nuruodo family|House Nuruodo]], [[Inrokini family|House Inrokini]], and [[Sabosen family|House Sabosen]]. This information seems to stem from the same New Republic sources mentioned above,<ref name="Gamer 5" /> which was confirmed by [[Jagged Fel]] shortly before the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Hunt for Zonama Sekot|search]] for the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Zonama Sekot/Legends|Zonama Sekot]] on Csilla<ref name="Force Heretic I">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic I: Remnant]]''</ref> in [[28 ABY/Legends|28 ABY]].<ref name="Force Heretic II date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic II: Refugee]]'' to [[28 ABY/Legends|28 ABY]].</ref>

[[File:Chisswomen.jpg|thumb|right|300px|"Bronze" and "Rust," female Chiss representatives of the Four Families]]
During the search, a Jedi delegation led by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] met with the members of the [[Council of Families]] in the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Ac'siel]] on Csilla, "[[Bronze (Chiss)|Bronze]]," "[[Rust]]," "[[Gray (Chiss)|Gray]]" and "[[Copper-green]]" among them, who wore bronze, rust-red, silver-gray and copper-green head-to-foot [[Robe/Legends|robes]] that respectively reflected the colors of their Families. During their meeting, the representatives debated whether to permit the delegation to pass through the Chiss Space, with two members being open to the idea. [[Chief Navigator]] [[Peita Aabe]], a representative from the Chiss Expansionary Defense Fleet, cast the deciding vote in favor of a compromise because the Council was unable to reach consensus. With unanimous approval from the Council, Aabe granted the delegation access to the [[Expeditionary Library]] for two [[Standard day/Legends|days]], while Gray presented them with [[Tris (Chiss)|Tris]], a guide from the Inrokini family.<ref name="Force Heretic II" />

According to the account offered by Aristocra [[Chaf'orm'bintrano]]<ref name="Dark Nest I" /> in [[35 ABY/Legends|35 ABY]],<ref name="Dark Nest I date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]'' to [[35 ABY/Legends|35 ABY]].</ref> the [[Third Vagaari War]] had caused a serious labor shortage among the Chiss (whether through casualties or simply due to conscription), and they turned to the insectoid [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]] for help, and hired several Nests as workers. Steps were taken to prevent any Chiss becoming [[Joiner]]s, but these were sabotaged, leading to the absorption of two Families into the Nests, while three others were unable to retain their position without the continued use of Killik labor.<ref name="Dark Nest I" />

Chaf'orm'bintrano claimed that this situation led to a "[[Chiss civil conflict|disagreement]]" in which the four other Families, assisted by [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Baron Fel]] and [[Syndic Mitth'raw'nuruodo's Household Phalanx]], removed the three Killik-dependent lineages from power. A [[Unidentified Chiss family|family]] of a [[Unidentified syndic (Ina'ganet'nuruodo)|syndic]] who opposed Fel's policies was destroyed by Soontir Fel during the conflict.<ref name="Dark Nest I" /> However, there are some uncertainties about the nature of this account. Firstly, it seems unlikely that there really were three wars between the Chiss and the Vagaari; secondly, the Aristocra himself supposedly belonged to the Chaf family, one of the lineages not mentioned in the lists of the four surviving families; his remarks also suggested that Baron Fel's family had adopted at least some of the trappings of a Ruling Family in their own right.

By [[41 ABY]],<ref name="TERC" /> the number of Ruling Families was once again nine. Though, which families returned to power was unknown.<ref name="Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref>

==Members==
[[File:Syndic_Zenta_of_House_Inrokini.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Syndic Zenta of House Inrokini]]
{{Quote|Just as our families are defined by their function in society, so are we defined by our roles as representatives of those families. We are here before you not as people, but as the beginning and end points of a decision-making process.|[[Bronze (Chiss)|Bronze]]|<ref name="Force Heretic II" />}}
===Yuuzhan Vong War and Dark Nest Crisis===
At the time of the Yuuzhan Vong War and the [[Dark Nest Crisis]], the Ruling Families included:
*[[Csapla family|Csapla]] (from [[Cioral/Legends|Cioral]]),<ref name="TEA" /> resource management and colonial affairs<ref name="Gamer 5" />
*[[Nuruodo family|Nuruodo]] (from [[Naporar/Legends|Naporar]]),<ref name="TEA" /> military and foreign policy<ref name="Gamer 5" />
*[[Inrokini family|Inrokini]] (from [[Csaus/Legends|Csaus]]),<ref name="TEA" /> Industry, non-military science, and communications<ref name="Gamer 5" />
*[[Sabosen family|Sabosen]] (from [[Sposia/Legends|Sposia]]),<ref name="TEA" /> law and order, health, education<ref name="Gamer 5" />

===Former Ruling Families===
At the time of the Yuuzhan Vong War and the Dark Nest Crisis, former Ruling Families included:
*[[First Ruling Family]]<ref name="Outbound Flight" />
*[[Chaf family/Legends|Chaf]]<ref name="Outbound Flight" /> (from [[Sarvchi/Legends|Sarvchi]])<ref name="TEA" />
*[[Mitth family/Legends|Mitth]]<ref name="Outbound Flight" /> (from [[Copero/Legends|Copero]])<ref name="TEA" />
*[[Brast family|Brast]]<ref name="Outbound Flight" />
*[[House Miurani|Miurani]]<ref name="SWTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>
*A [[Unidentified Chiss family|family]]<ref name="Dark Nest I" />

The outlying colonies of [[Sharb/Legends|Sharb]], [[Noris/Legends|Noris]], [[Schesa/Legends|Schesa]], [[Ornfra/Legends|Ornfra]], [[Catlia]] and [[Massoss/Legends|Massoss]], homes to former Ruling Families, were largely wiped out prior to the [[Swarm War]]. Two of the Families who resided on the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] Catlia and Massoss respectively became Joiners in the [[The Colony|Colony]], while the others fell on a losing side of a civil conflict.<ref name="TEA" />
